v1.feedback: The Aizawa-to-hushed chain logic is genuine — parameter d ramp tightens the orbit mathematically rather than just rescaling, and the 45s cycle is appropriately unhurried. However the hush envelope is almost imperceptibly subtle: 6% spatial contraction and 15% luminance drop may not register as an event to a viewer who doesn't know to look. Consider deepening the contraction to 12-15% and letting the indigo shift dominate more (uHush * 0.55 instead of 0.35) so the held-breath moment is readable within 2 seconds of arrival. The centroid-tracking camera drift is a nice touch but verify at default zoom that the attractor fills enough frame — z=22 with scale 3.6 may leave the form a bit small.

v2.feedback: The hush-breath cycle is a genuinely good chain move — same Aizawa skeleton as the parent but the 45s contraction/dimming reads as 'the room after ta-da.' Palette (sage, violet, indigo, ash, bone) is well-restrained and the luminance drop during contraction is tasteful. Two refinements: the 14% spatial contraction and 32% luminance drop may be too subtle on most monitors — consider deepening the contraction to ~22% and letting the bloom strength also breathe (drop to near zero at hush-peak) so the silence reads more dramatically. Second, the Aizawa is becoming familiar territory in this gallery; a future chain from this piece should push the attractor toward a less-seen parameter regime or let the hush phase partially dissolve the form into sparse dust before reconstitution.
